title: Engineer turns Claude Code into a UK tax-law research agent over ~10,000 documents
summary: Martin Alderson had Claude Code scrape UK legislation and HMRC tax manuals into folders, then repurposed CLAUDE.md with research instructions so the agent could search the corpus to answer tax-policy questions.
agent_role: Claude Code wrote the recursive scraper, built the document corpus and searched it to answer questions; Alderson designed the setup and judged the answers.
what_they_did: Martin Alderson used Claude Code to write a recursive scraper. It downloaded UK tax legislation and HMRC's Corporation Tax and Personal Tax manuals into folders, about 10,000 text documents. He then rewrote CLAUDE.md, refining it with Claude Code, to cast it as an expert UK tax professional. The file tells it to launch parallel subagents (corporate law, personal tax, current rates, anti-avoidance, legislation) that write research files, then combine them in output.md. He tested it on past ATT exam questions.
how_it_went: After about 5 minutes the agent wrote its answer. He gives it 2.5 out of 3 marks, missing one residency detail. He says plain Opus got the same first question completely wrong.
worth_knowing: The folder doesn't need to be well organised, though he suspects better structure would improve results. The main barrier is that Claude Code runs in a terminal, which puts off non-technical users.
prompt: Write a scraper that recursively downloads the reference documents for [domain, e.g. UK tax] from [source websites] as text files into folders. Then draft a CLAUDE.md that makes you an expert in [domain] who answers questions from non-technical users using only this folder. For each question, launch parallel subagents for [research areas]. Each one writes findings to research_[topic].md, and you consolidate an answer with citations in output.md. Show me the CLAUDE.md for review before we test it on [sample question].

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
